newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Stable in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Stable in listless trade.

text.p: Singapore's naphtha steadied in listless trade ahead of a Labour day holiday while mogas was supported by firm bids, traders said on Wednesday.
They said a fall in Singapore's light distillates stocks failed to boost prices.
Singapore ligth distillates stocks, comprising gasoline, naphtha and reformate fell by 277,000 barrels to 7.266 million barrels, the Trade Development Board said.
Near market close, a European major sold a 50,000-barrel cargo of 97 octane gasoline for May loading to a Dutch trader at $24.75 per barrel on a free-on board Singapore basis.
Traders said the market was propped up by the firm bid.
"The market fundamental is not that strong," said another trader. "There is just no demand except for Taiwan."

Taiwan has just issued a tender to buy unleaded 95-octane reformate for delivery in June 11-30. The tender which closes May 5 and is valid for two days, seeks a 250,000 barrel cargo on a cost and freight basis for delivery to Keelung, Kaohsiung and Shalung.
Late Tuesday, a Japanese trader purchased a 95 octane unleaded cargo at $24.05 per barrel from local trader for May 24-28.
The naphtha market was quiet ahead of the Labour Day holiday on Thursday, traders said.
Naphtha swaps for May and June were quoted at $21.45/$21.55 and $21.55/$21.65o with May unchanged at $21.35/$21.55 per barrel and June at $21.45/$21.65.
Traders said the market lacks support with North Asian demand still weak with most ethylene plant still undergoing turnarounds.
Some spot buying interests were heard from Thailand for June delivery but traders said current supplies were more than sufficient to meet that demand.
